question.problem:
The output voltage of laptop AC adapters is normally distributed with a mean of $19$ volts and a standard deviation $0.05$ volts. What is the probability that the output voltage of a randomly selected adapter is less than $18.97$ volts?

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-0.8\,$ | $\,0.2119\,$ | $\,0.2090\,$ | $\,0.2061\,$ |
| $\,-0.7\,$ | $\,0.2420\,$ | $\,0.2389\,$ | $\,0.2358\,$ |
| $\,-0.6\,$ | $\,0.2743\,$ | $\,0.2709\,$ | $\,0.2676\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the voltage (in volts) of a randomly selected adapter. Then we have $X∼N(19,{0.05}^{2}).$

We want to find $P(X<18.97).$ First, we write this as a cumulative probability:

$$
P(X<18.97)=P(X\le 18.97)
$$

Then, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 18.97) & =P(Z\le \frac{18.97-19}{0.05}) \\  & =P(Z\le -0.6) \\  & =Φ(-0.6)\end{aligned}
$$

From the $z$-table, we see that

$$
Φ(-0.6)=0.2743≈0.27.
$$

Therefore, the probability that the output voltage of a randomly selected adapter is less than $18.97$ volts is approximately $0.27.$
